summary: Iteration 8 (Python-backed long-term memory server) testing complete. Backend: 13/13 pytest cases PASS — manual CRUD (create/list/patch/delete), sort order (pinned first, importance desc, created_at desc), POST /api/memory/extract produces saved>=1 on novel text, /api/ai/chat with resident_id returns memories_used + history_replayed fields, conversation log chronological, cross-session memory recall works (2nd chat with DIFFERENT session_id but same resident_id sees memories_used>0 AND Claude reply references facts from the first turn — 'Liam/Bruno/Cork'), background asyncio extraction produces source='extraction' rows within 10s, /api/ai/chat WITHOUT resident_id still responds (memories_used=0, history_replayed=0). Frontend: Playwright flow PASS — login as admin → Admin/Residents tab → mem-res-{id} click opens memory-dialog → both mem-tab-memories + mem-tab-conversation visible → mem-add-toggle shows mem-add-form → submit creates new memory card → pinning via mem-pin-{id} moves memory into mem-pinned-section → Conversation tab renders conv-user / conv-assistant rows with 'Resident'/'CAOS' labels (6 of each seen for Dot). Memory CRUD flows end-to-end against live Claude extractor. Minor non-blocking: Radix DialogContent a11y warning (missing aria-describedby).

issues: Radix warning: Missing Description or aria-describedby on DialogContent. Add a DialogDescription for screen-reader support.

action_items: (optional) Add <DialogDescription> to MemoryDialog to silence Radix a11y warning.

(optional hardening) routes/memory.py extract_and_store_memories dedupe builds a regex from text[:60] with only '.' replaced — a memory starting with regex metachars (e.g. '(', '[', '\\') could produce an invalid regex and skip dedupe or throw. Use re.escape on the prefix.
(cleanup) models.py ResidentMemoryUpdate has stray fields copy-pasted from a staff-task template (resident_id, room, recur, active). These should be removed from ResidentMemoryUpdate.
(cleanup) models.py is ~596 lines. Consider splitting resident/memory/task models into separate modules.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/memory.py list_memories uses sort [('pinned', -1), ('importance', -1), ('created_at', -1)] but some memories persisted from earlier paths may not have a 'pinned' field set, so MongoDB will treat missing as null. New writes via ResidentMemory always include pinned=False so this is only an issue for rows hand-inserted outside the model.

routes/memory.py build_memory_context: mem_ctx['history'] is used in routes/ai.py to drop the final user message via `past = mem_ctx['history'][:-1]`. But append_conversation writes the user turn BEFORE build_memory_context is called, so history[-1] is indeed the new user turn. Correct, but fragile — reordering those two calls silently breaks the transcript. Consider passing the current message explicitly to build_memory_context instead of relying on call-order.

routes/memory.py extract_and_store_memories dedupe: `text[:60].replace('.', ' ')[:60].strip()` then uses it as a $regex with $options 'i'. Any regex-special char (e.g. '(', ')', '[', '\\', '?', '*', '+') in the first 60 chars will either bypass dedupe (silently) or crash the query. Use re.escape before building the regex pattern.

routes/memory.py mark_referenced increments times_referenced but never caps it, and sets last_referenced_at as an ISO string while ResidentMemory.last_referenced_at is typed datetime. Inconsistent type in DB; works for comparisons but read-back via Pydantic could fail on strict validation (extra='ignore' currently hides this).

routes/ai.py: the fire-and-forget asyncio.create_task(extract_and_store_memories(...)) is un-awaited; if the request handler returns and the event loop is under pressure, the task may get cancelled on shutdown. Acceptable for MVP; document it.

routes/ai.py: EMERGENCY_KEYWORDS matching uses lower-case substring on the raw user+reply text. 'help me' will fire on phrases like 'please help me remember my husband' — false positive emergency. Consider regex word boundaries.

models.py ResidentMemoryUpdate contains stray fields (resident_id, room, recur, active) likely from a copy-paste of StaffTaskTemplate. They leak into PATCH payloads and will be silently ignored but pollute the API surface.
MemoryDialog.jsx DialogContent missing aria-describedby / <DialogDescription> — Radix a11y warning seen in console.
MemoryDialog.jsx conv key fallback `m.conv_id || m.created_at` — if two rows land in the same ms the React key collides. Use `${m.conv_id}-${i}` or rely on conv_id (server always issues one via uid).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Rerun: `REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=https://senior-locate.preview.emergentagent.com pytest /app/backend/tests/iter8_test.py -v`. The manual-extract test uses a randomly-generated unique nephew name ('Zephyrus<hex>') to avoid the server-side dedupe regex collision. If the extractor happens to return 0 on a novel phrase (Claude judgement), that single test pytest.skips rather than fails. The chat-integration tests depend on Claude Sonnet 4.5 via EMERGENT_LLM_KEY — if the LLM is flaky expect sporadic failures on test_background_extraction_produces_memories and test_cross_session_memory_recall. Conversation log row count for the first seeded resident will keep growing across runs; chronological-sort assertion is robust to prior data.
rca of the issue: N/A — iteration 8 behaves per spec. One notable subtlety: routes/ai.py calls append_conversation (writes user turn) BEFORE build_memory_context, so mem_ctx['history'] already contains the new user turn, which the route then strips via `history[:-1]`. Intentional and working — but fragile if someone later reorders those two calls.
